# generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.

## Rival: count nearest seed cells instead of nearest colors

`tie_by_seed` computes the same wall-aware cardinal distances, but leaves a blank
whenever two or more *seed cells* share the minimum distance—even when their
colors agree. The intended rule only leaves a tie blank when **distinct colors**
share the minimum. This rival is stronger than ignoring walls or using diagonal
distance because it preserves almost all of the intended computation and fits
all four canonical pairs (three demonstrations plus the saved canonical test).
All canonical seed colors are distinct, so those examples cannot separate the
two interpretations. The additional `first_seed_only` rival also fits 4/4.

## Exact generated counterexample

Final generator `1b860d59e505465a7266b509834a2d30fa94ff883bb2b8659bafbf1c7e533f83`; seed `99100`, sample index `0`, difficulty `easy`, overrides
`{}`. Each row below is a row of integer cells, not an encoded alternative input:

```text
0000009000000
0050080000000
0050000000000
5055555055555
0050100000000
0001000000000
0050000000000
0050000000000
0250000000000
```

At zero-based **(row 4, column 3)**, the neighboring seeds at `(4,4)` and `(5,3)`
are both color 1 and both one step away. The actual Racket output is **1**; the
rival output is **0**. The complete integer grid and both full outputs are in
`checks/counterexample.json`; the canonical fits and Racket provenance are in
`checks/voronoi-probe.json`. The input passes the final validator.

The authoring probe calls the public `Catalog.apply`, with unchanged canonical
pin `cb6c4f271562`; the report retains Racket metadata, hashes and the exact
command. Its independent Racket comparison has zero mismatches in 40 cases:
4 canonical inputs plus easy/medium/hard draws at seeds 99100..99111, indices
0..11. The 300-draw input-only probe separately finds same-color tie witnesses
51/100 times in each band (seeds 99100..99199, indices 0..99).

## Does the proposal emit and teach it?

Yes: the grid above is an ordinary default draw, not a hand-inserted fixture.
The repeated/repeated/four-seeds/four-seeds schedule plus witness-conditioned
sampling ensures at least two such witnesses in any default four-draw window.
Therefore every three-demo/one-query rotation retains a refutation in the demos.
The Racket-backed production census found no ambiguity in 300 lessons or 1,200
rotations over 1,200 unique inputs, with five declared rivals. The separate cyclic
Python tests cover 32 starts in each band. Explicit overrides requesting all
seeds have different colors do not carry this lesson guarantee. No result here
claims uniqueness against every possible undeclared rule.
